text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the rash or joint pain start immediately after beginning the amoxicillin, or was there a delay of several days? Also, have you noticed any swelling in her joints or any changes in her urine output?

I need to clarify if she has experienced any swelling of the face or hands, or if her rash appears as raised, reddish-purple spots (purpura) rather than flat hives. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal urinalysis makes IgA vasculitis less likely, so I suspect a serum sickness-like reaction. Does she have any swelling of her face or hands, and are the joints visibly swollen or just painful?

speaker: Patient

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the timing of symptoms starting one week after amoxicillin initiation, the presence of urticarial rash, joint pain, and low-grade fever, this clinical picture is classic for a serum sickness-like reaction. DIAGNOSIS READY: Serum sickness-like reaction
